text:
## Step 5: Standing Order Execution  
### Scheduled Processing  
**Timing:**
- Standing order executes on scheduled date (e.g., 15th of month)
- Processing occurs early morning (before business hours)
- Funds transferred via FPS (Faster Payments Service)
- Recipient account receives funds within 1 hour  
**Execution Process:**
1. System identifies standing orders due
2. Validates source account has sufficient funds
3. Initiates FPS transfer
4. Records transaction in ledger
5. Updates standing order status (completed)
6. Notifies customer (optional, if opted in)  
**If Funds Unavailable:**
- Transfer fails (declined)
- Customer notified of failure
- Retry attempt made (usually once)
- Manual intervention if persistent failure

raw_entities.description: End-to-end process for executing scheduled standing order payments on a customer account. Executes on the scheduled date (e.g., 15th of month) during early morning hours before business hours, with funds transferred via Faster Payments Service (FPS) to the recipient account within 1 hour. Includes validation of sufficient funds, transaction recording, status updates, and customer notification.

raw_entities.description: Automated system step that identifies all standing orders scheduled for execution on the current processing date.

context: Validates source account has sufficient funds

raw_entities.name: FPS Transfer Initiation
raw_entities.description: System step that initiates the Faster Payments Service (FPS) transfer to move funds from the source account to the recipient account.

raw_entities.name: Transaction Ledger Recording
raw_entities.description: System step that records the executed standing order transaction in the account ledger for audit and reconciliation purposes.

raw_entities.name: Standing Order Status Update
aliases: Update Standing Order Status to Completed
raw_entities.description: System step that updates the standing order record to reflect completion of the current execution cycle.

raw_entities.name: Customer Notification of Execution
aliases: Notify Customer of Standing Order Execution
raw_entities.description: Optional notification step that informs the customer of successful standing order execution, triggered only if the customer has opted in to receive such notifications.

raw_entities.name: Transfer Failure Handling
raw_entities.description: Exception handling step executed when the source account lacks sufficient funds to complete the standing order transfer, resulting in transfer decline.

raw_entities.name: Retry Attempt for Failed Transfer
raw_entities.description: Exception handling step that automatically attempts to retry the failed standing order transfer, typically executed once before escalation to manual intervention.

raw_entities.name: Manual Intervention for Persistent Failure
raw_entities.description: Manual intervention step triggered when standing order transfer fails persistently despite automatic retry attempts, requiring human review and resolution.

raw_entities.name: Automated Standing Order Processing System
raw_entities.description: Automated system responsible for identifying due standing orders, validating funds, initiating FPS transfers, recording transactions, updating status, and handling retry logic for failed transfers.
context: Validates source account has sufficient funds

raw_entities.name: Customer Service Operations Team
raw_entities.description: Human operations team responsible for manual intervention when standing order transfers fail persistently and require human review and resolution.

raw_entities.description: Decision gate that determines whether the source account contains sufficient funds to execute the standing order transfer. Pass path leads to FPS transfer initiation; fail path triggers transfer decline and customer notification.

raw_entities.name: Transfer Success Confirmation Decision
raw_entities.description: Decision gate that confirms whether the FPS transfer completed successfully. Pass path leads to transaction recording and status update; fail path triggers retry logic and eventual manual intervention if persistent.
